facts.statement: The genus Ichthyornis was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1872.
facts.quote: authority: Marsh, 1872

facts.statement: Ichthyornis was discovered in 1870 by Benjamin Franklin Mudge in the North Fork of the Solomon River in Kansas.
facts.quote: Ichthyornis was discovered in 1870 by Benjamin Franklin Mudge, a professor from Kansas State Agricultural College who recovered the initial fossils from the North Fork of the Solomon River in Kansas, United States.

facts.statement: Fossils of Ichthyornis are found in the Western Interior Seaway deposits across Alberta, Alabama, Kansas, New Mexico, Saskatchewan, and Texas.
facts.quote: Its fossil remains are mostly known from the chalks of Alberta, Alabama, Kansas (Greenhorn Limestone), New Mexico, Saskatchewan, and Texas, in strata that were laid down in the Western Interior Seaway

facts.statement: Ichthyornis lived during the Late Cretaceous, from the Cenomanian to the Campanian ages.
facts.quote: spanning from the Cenomanian to the Campanian ages of the Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: Ichthyornis is an extinct genus of toothed, seabird-like ornithuran named for its fish-like vertebrae.
facts.quote: Ichthyornis (meaning "fish bird", after its fish-like vertebrae) is an extinct genus of toothy seabird-like ornithuran

facts.statement: Ichthyornis is thought to have been the Cretaceous equivalent of modern seabirds like gulls, petrels, and skimmers.
facts.quote: It is thought that Ichthyornis was the Cretaceous ecological equivalent of modern seabirds such as gulls, petrels, and skimmers.

facts.statement: An average Ichthyornis specimen was about 24 cm long with a skeletal wingspan of approximately 43 cm.
facts.quote: An average specimen was the size of a pigeon, 24 cm long, with a skeletal wingspan (not taking feathers into account) of around 43 cm

facts.statement: Ichthyornis had teeth only in the middle of its jaws, while the tips were toothless and covered by a beak.
facts.quote: The teeth were present only in the middle portion of the upper and lower jaws. The jaw tips had no teeth and were covered in a beak.

facts.statement: The beak of Ichthyornis was compound, made of several distinct plates similar to an albatross, unlike the single keratin sheet of most modern birds.
facts.quote: The beak of Ichthyornis, like the hesperornithids, was compound and made up of several distinct plates, similar to the beak of an albatross, rather than a single sheet of keratin as in most modern birds.

facts.statement: Ichthyornis teeth were flattened, wider at the base, curved backward, and lacked serrations.
facts.quote: The teeth were more flattened than the rounded teeth found in crocodilians, though they became wider towards the base of the crown. The tips of the teeth were curved backward and lacked any serrations.

facts.statement: Ichthyornis possessed modern wings and a breastbone indicating strong flight, placing it in the advanced group Carinatae.
facts.quote: The wings and breastbone were very modern in appearance, suggesting strong flight ability and placing it with modern birds in the advanced group Carinatae.

facts.statement: Studies of Ichthyornis brain casts show it had a relatively basal brain similar to Archaeopteryx and non-avian theropods.
facts.quote: A study on an Ichthyornis endocast reveals that it had a relatively basal brain compared to modern birds, similar to that of Archaeopteryx and other non-avian theropods.

facts.statement: Ichthyornis had a palate that was remarkably similar to that of modern neognath birds.
facts.quote: Conversely, it had a palate remarkably convergent with that of modern neognaths.

facts.statement: Earlier Ichthyornis remains date to the early Turonian (about 93 million years ago) in Kansas and the late Cenomanian in Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: Even earlier remains attributed to Ichthyornis have been found in the Greenhorn Formation of Kansas, dating to the early Turonian age (about 93 million years ago), and the late Cenomanian age of Saskatchewan, Canada.

facts.statement: Ichthyornis specimens from earlier eras were generally smaller than those from later periods.
facts.quote: Specimens of Ichthyornis from earlier eras were, on average, smaller than later ones.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh secured the naming rights to Ichthyornis from his rival Edward Drinker Cope after intercepting the fossil shipment.
facts.quote: Marsh had narrowly won the prestige of studying and naming the important fossil at the expense of his rival.

facts.statement: Marsh initially thought the toothed jaws belonged to a separate marine reptile named Colonosaurus mudgei before realizing they belonged to the bird.
facts.quote: Marsh considered the unusual vertebrae of the bird to resemble those of a fish, so he named it Ichthyornis, or "fish bird." Later in 1872, Marsh described the toothed jaws as a new species of marine reptile, named Colonosaurus mudgei after their discoverer.

facts.statement: As late as 1952, J.T. Gregory debated that the toothed jaws belonged to a small mosasaur related to Clidastes rather than the bird.
facts.quote: The similarity of the lower jaw and teeth to those of mosasaurs is so great that as late as 1952, J.T. Gregory argued that it really belonged to a diminutive species or young individual related to the genus Clidastes.

facts.statement: Accusations that Marsh tampered with fossils or created a hoax by combining reptilian jaws with a bird body persisted until at least 1967.
facts.quote: Many accused Marsh of having tampered with the fossils or intentionally created a hoax by associating reptilian jaws with the body of a bird, accusations that continued to surface even as late as 1967.

facts.statement: Marsh classified Ichthyornis in the new subclass Odontornithes and order Ichthyornithes due to its unique concave vertebrae and teeth.
facts.quote: Due to the previously unknown features of Ichthyornis (vertebrae concave on either side and teeth), Marsh chose to classify it in an entirely new sub-class of birds he called the Odontornithes (or "toothed birds"), and in the new order Ichthyornithes (later Ichthyornithiformes).

facts.statement: Charles Darwin stated in 1880 that Ichthyornis offered the best support for his theory of evolution since 1859.
facts.quote: Darwin himself told Marsh in an 1880 letter that Ichthyornis and Hesperornis offered "the best support for the theory of evolution" since he had first published On the Origin of Species in 1859.

facts.statement: Ichthyornis was an extinct genus of toothed birds from the Late Cretaceous whose name means "fish-bird" due to vertebrae resembling those of fish.
facts.quote: Ichthyornis (gr. "ave-pez" debido a sus vértebras similares a las de los peces) es un género de aves dentadas extintas del Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Ichthyornis lived in North America between 93 and 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: hace entre 93 y 75 millones de años que habitaron en América del Norte

facts.statement: Ichthyornis was the first toothed bird discovered, and Charles Darwin noted its significance during the early development of his theory of evolution.
facts.quote: Fue la primera ave con dientes en ser descubierta, y Charles Darwin notó su significado durante los primeros años de desarrollo de la teoría de la evolución

facts.statement: Ichthyornis had an average size similar to a pigeon, measuring 24 centimeters in length with a wingspan of about 43 centimeters excluding feather length.
facts.quote: Tenía un tamaño promedio similar al de una paloma, de 24 centímetros de largo, con una envergadura alar (sin contar la longitud de las plumas que tenía en vida) de cerca de 43 cm

facts.statement: Ichthyornis is notable for having concave vertebrae in both the front and rear sections, a feature similar to that of some fish.
facts.quote: Ichthyornis es notable sobre todo por la combinación de vértebras cóncavas tanto en la zona frontal como trasera de las mismas (similar a algunos peces, de los que el ave obtuvo su nombre)

facts.statement: The teeth of Ichthyornis were more flattened than the rounded teeth seen in crocodiles, becoming wider toward the base of the crown.
facts.quote: Los dientes eran más aplanados que los dientes más redondeados que se observan en los cocodrilos, aunque se vuelven más amplios hacia la base de la corona

facts.statement: The tips of Ichthyornis teeth were curved backward and lacked serrated edges.
facts.quote: La punta de los dientes estaba curvada hacia atrás y carecía de bordes aserrados

facts.statement: The beak of Ichthyornis was composed of several distinct plates similar to an albatross, rather than the single layer of keratin found in many modern birds.
facts.quote: El pico de Ichthyornis, como el de las hesperornítidas y otras aves primitivas, estaba compuesto por varias placas distintas, similar al pico de un albatros, en lugar de la capa única de queratina que tienen muchas aves modernas

facts.statement: Ichthyornis is thought to have been the ecological equivalent of modern seabirds like gulls, petrels, and shearwaters during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Se piensa que Ichthyornis era el equivalente ecológico en el Cretácico de las modernas aves marinas como gaviotas, petreles y rayadores

facts.statement: Unlike more primitive birds such as Enantiornithes, Ichthyornis appears to have reached adulthood through a short and continuous growth process.
facts.quote: A diferencia de aves más primitivas como las Enantiornithes, parece que llegaba a la adultez en un proceso de crecimiento corto y continuo

facts.statement: Older fossils attributed to Ichthyornis have been found in the Greenhorn Formation of Kansas dating to the early Turonian (about 93 million years ago) and in Saskatchewan dating to the Cenomanian (about 95 million years ago).
facts.quote: Restos aún más antiguos atribuidos a Ichthyornis han sido encontrados en la formación Greenhorn de Kansas, datando de principios del periodo Turoniense (hace cerca de 93 millones de años), y el periodo Cenomaniense de Saskatchewan, datando de hace unos 95 millones de años

facts.statement: A full re-description of Ichthyornis specimens was published by paleontologist Julia Clarke in 2004.
facts.quote: A full re-description of these specimens was published by paleontologist Julia Clarke in 2004

facts.statement: In Julia Clarke's 2004 review, the former order Ichthyornithiformes and family Ichthyornithidae were superseded by the clade Ichthyornithes.
facts.quote: In Clarke's 2004 review, the former order Ichthyornithiformes and the family Ichthyornithidae are now superseded by the clade Ichthyornithes

facts.statement: The genus Ichthyornis was named by Marsh in 1872.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Marsh, 1872

facts.statement: The only currently recognized species of Ichthyornis is I. dispar.
facts.quote: species: I. dispar

facts.statement: Ichthyornis was originally discovered in 1870 by Benjamin Franklin Mudge, who recovered fossils from the Solomon River in Kansas, USA.
facts.quote: Ichthyornis fue descubierto originariamente en 1870 por Benjamin Franklin Mudge, un profesor del Kansas State Agricultural College quien recuperó los fósiles del río Solomon en Kansas, EUA.

facts.statement: In 1872, Othniel Charles Marsh offered to identify any relevant fossils for free and give Mudge full credit for the discovery.
facts.quote: Marsh escribió a Mudge en 1872 y le ofreció identificar cualquier fósil relevante sin costo alguno, y le daría a Mudge todo el crédito por el descubrimiento.

facts.statement: Marsh narrowly won the prestige of studying and naming the important fossil at the expense of his rival.
facts.quote: Marsh había ganado por poco el prestigio de estudiar y nombrar el importante fósil a expensas de su rival.

facts.statement: Marsh named the bird Ichthyornis, meaning "fish bird," because its unusual vertebrae resembled those of a fish.
facts.quote: Marsh consideró que las vértebras inusuales del ave se parecían a las de un pez, por lo que la nombró Ichthyornis, o "ave pez."

facts.statement: In 1873, Marsh realized his mistake after preparing cranial bones and found that the toothed jaws belonged to the bird itself, not a marine reptile.
facts.quote: En 1873, Marsh pronto reconoció su error. A través de la preparación y exposición de los huesos craneales de la roca, él halló que las mandíbulas dentadas provenían del ave misma y no de un reptil marino.

facts.statement: Due to its unique features like concave vertebrae on both sides and teeth, Marsh classified the bird into its own subclass called Odontornithes, meaning "toothed birds," and the new order Ichthyornithes (later Ichthyornithiformes).
facts.quote: Debido a las peculiares características del Ichthyornis (vértebras cóncavas en ambos lados y dientes), Marsh escogió clasificar el ave en una subclase propia que llamó Odontornithes (es decir, "aves dentadas" en griego), y en el nuevo orden Ichthyornithes (más tarde Ichthyornithiformes).

facts.statement: In 1880, Darwin wrote to Marsh that Ichthyornis and Hesperornis offered "the best support for the theory of evolution" since the publication of On the Origin of Species in 1859.
facts.quote: Darwin comentó a Marsh en una carta en 1880 que Ichthyornis y Hesperornis ofrecían "el mejor soporte para la teoría de la evolución" desde la primera publicación de El origen de las especies en 1859.

facts.statement: Many accused Marsh of altering fossils or intentionally creating a hoax by associating reptilian jaws with a bird's body, accusations that continued as late as 1967.
facts.quote: Muchos acusaron a Marsh de haber alterado los fósiles o crear intencionalmente un trucaje asociando mandíbulas reptilianas con el cuerpo de un ave,acusaciones que continuaron incluso hasta una fecha tardía como 1967.

facts.statement: However, an overwhelming majority of researchers have demonstrated that Marsh's interpretation of the fossils was correct, and he has been fully vindicated by later findings.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, una abrumadora mayoría de investigadores han demostrado que la interpretación de Marsh de los fósiles era correcta, y él ha sido totalmente reivindicado por hallazgos posteriores.

facts.statement: In 1997, the situation became so confusing that Jacques Gauthier, the curator of the museum's vertebrate paleontology collection, authorized the dismantling of both panels.
facts.quote: En 1997, la situación se volvió tan confusa que Jacques Gauthier, el actual curador de la colección paleontológica de vertebrados del museo, autorizó la desmantelación de ambos paneles.

facts.statement: A complete redescription of these specimens was published by paleontologist Julia Clarke in 2004.
facts.quote: Una redescripción completa de estos especímenes fue publicada por la paleontóloga Julia Clarke en 2004.

facts.statement: Ichthyornis is close to the ancestors of modern birds, the Neornithes, but represents an independent lineage.
facts.quote: Ichthyornis es cercano a los ancestros de las aves modernas, las Neornithes, pero representa un linaje independiente.

facts.statement: In Clarke's 2004 review, the former order Ichthyornithiformes and family Ichthyornithidae were replaced by the subclass Ichthyornithes, defined phylogenetically as all descendants of the most recent common ancestor of Ichthyornis dispar and modern birds.
facts.quote: En la revisión de Clarke en 2004, el antiguo orden Ichthyornithiformes y la familia Ichthyornithidae son ahora sustituidos por la subclase Ichthyornithes, que en el artículo fue también definida de acuerdo a la clasificación filogenética como todos los descendientes del más reciente ancestro común de Ichthyornis dispar y las aves modernas.

facts.statement: Of the several described species, only one, Ichthyornis dispar, is currently recognized, following Julia Clarke's monumental review.
facts.quote: De las varias especies descritas, solo una, Ichthyornis dispar, es actualmente reconocida, siguiendo la monumental revisión de Julia Clarke.

facts.statement: Michael Mortimer noted that this is incorrect; although I. anceps cannot become the type species of Ichthyornis, the ICZN does not prevent it from becoming the oldest synonym of the type species I. dispar.
facts.quote: Michael Mortimer ha anotado que esto es incorrecto; aunque I. anceps no puede llegar a ser la especie tipo de Ichthyornis, el ICZN no le impide convertirse en el sinónimo más antiguo de la especie tipo I. dispar.

facts.statement: The similarity of the lower jaw and teeth to those of mosasaurs (marine fish-eating lizards) was so great that as late as 1952, it was claimed they actually belonged to a diminutive species or juvenile individuals of the genus Clidastes or a related genus.
facts.quote: La similitud de la mandíbula inferior y los dientes a los de los mosasaurios (lagartos marinos piscívoros) es tan grande que incluso en una fecha tardía como 1952, se afirmaba que realmente pertenecían a una especie diminuta o a individuos jóvenes del género Clidastes o un género relacionado con éste.

facts.statement: "Ichthyornis" minusculus from the Bissekty Formation (Late Cretaceous) of Kyzyl Kum, Uzbekistan, is probably an enantiornithine.
facts.quote: "Ichthyornis" minusculus de la formación Bissekty (Cretácico Superior) de Kyzyl Kum, Uzbekistán, es probablemente una enantiornita.
